paragraphs.source_en:
With wild thyme and the gadding vine o’ergrown,
And all their echoes mourn.
 This line recalls the opening stanza of Gray’s Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard (cp. Unused
stanzas for Adonais L, Longman iv 338–9, ll. 2–4 and note):
The curfew tolls the knell of parting day,
The lowing herd wind slowly o’er the lea,
The ploughman homeward plods his weary way,
And leaves the world to darkness and to me.
 day,] day; Adonais (1821), Adonais (1829), 1829, 1839, and subsequent eds. The draft in Nbk 20 has
no punctuation after day, and a cancelled draft of the following l. 132 reading For she can mimic not,
showing that the Since clause goes with the preceding and not the following lines (see BSM vii 310–11).
 132–4. more dear . . . all sounds] Echo, who pined for unrequited love of Narcissus, loved Adonais’s
poetry more even than she loved the lips of Narcissus.
 she] they 1834, 1839 (evidence for 1834 as printer’s copy for 1839).
